title: Touring with Elvin in Europe, South America and the US
summary: Mostly Europe, a US Information Service tour of South America, Japan and a few US clubs.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Am I correct that you worked with him more in Europe than you did in the states?

Yeah. We did mostly Europe. We did a lot of European festivals: Italy, the first tour I did was Sweden, Italy. We played Ronnie Scott’s every year. The same as Buddy’s band. Buddy would play Ronnie Scott’s. Elvin would play Ronnie Scott’s. We worked all through Europe. We did South America, we did a tour down there in 197 — I can’t remember. In the 70s. This was when, we went down for the CIA it was like a branch of the CIA called the US Information Service. They sent us to every trouble spot in South America, right? So we went to Uruguay, Paraguay, Chile, Medellin, Bogota, Guayaquil, Santiago. You know, every place where there was some — they sent us down as kind of a peace thing. So we went there with that. We went to Japan with Elvin. In the states we always had a circuit. We would work the Vanguard two or three times a year. We worked a jazz showcase in Chicago. I don’t remember — we worked a couple of other places in Detroit, Baker’s Keyboard Lounge. There were some other spotty places that we would work but that’s about it. There were only a few places. I don’t remember — California we’d work the Jazz Bakery. But there wasn’t a lot of activity going on at that time.
